cells.tense: Right now you're the one deciding what gets tended, and you're present to the choosing.
cells.ask: name one thing that's finished enough to let go of, and let one person witness it
cells.core: This is the part of your life where things actually get completed. You're holding two demands at once without dropping either, and you know which one needs water this morning and which one needs to be left alone. What you've been building is arriving, and it's arriving because you kept showing up to it. The care isn't exhausting you right now. That's the sign it's working.\n\nWhat's left is to say that out loud somewhere. The completion is real, and it's ready to be witnessed. Release isn't a loss here — it's what the finishing was always for. Let one person stand next to the finished thing and see it with you.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending what you built, and it's finally coming to completion.
cells.verb: tending what grows with steady, responsible care
cells.place: the point of departure that is also arrival — where what's been built can finally be released into what comes next

cells.tense: You're living at the far edge of what hasn't happened yet — bracing for the release before the thing is finished.
cells.ask: pause the next move and stay with one thing that's already complete, long enough to actually feel finished
cells.core: When this part of your life is going well, the care doesn't run you down. You hold what needs holding, you let the rest go quiet, and what you've tended completes on its own time. You can feel when something is done. But right now you're pushing the finish harder than the work asks for. Before anything has fully arrived, you're already rehearsing the next round — what it will mean, what might go wrong, whether it will hold. The bracing has replaced the tending.\n\nWhat you're after is the rest that comes after being truly done with something, not another thing started. The way back is to sit inside one thing that's already finished until you can feel it as finished. Let the satisfaction come from what's here, not from what you've already lined up next.

cells.tense: You stopped tending a while back, and you're still standing where the tending stopped.
cells.ask: go back to one small thing you already tend well — water it once more, and let that be enough for now
cells.core: This is the part of your life where things are meant to complete and release. When it's working, care doesn't exhaust you. You hold what needs holding, you let the rest go quiet, and what you've been growing reaches its own finish. Right now the care has stalled. The finishing stopped, and the unfinished thing is sitting exactly where you left it.\n\nWhat will bring you back isn't more effort pushed into the empty spaces. It's going to one small piece of work you already know how to do, tending it once more, and letting that be the whole of today. The hope for what this could become is still there — somewhere it's still burning. Let it light the one small tending, not the whole abandoned field.

cells.tense: You're the one doing the tending, but you're describing it as if it were just happening around you.
cells.ask: name one thing you finished by hand, and let someone see it was you who finished it
cells.core: When this part of your life is going well, you know what you're carrying. You decide what gets kept and what gets released, and the deciding shows in the finished thing. That's still happening here. You're already in the middle of the completion — you're the one who knows when the work is done and who it's for. But somewhere along the way the doing became invisible to you, and you talk about the outcome as if it arrived on its own.\n\nSay one such thing plainly, to someone. Name what you finished with your own hands. That's not taking credit — it's the finishing being seen for what it is, which is what the completion was always reaching toward.
